checks.message: 120 signers, each in exactly one split (genuine specimens train/val/test: 80/20/20)

0 of 120 signers have two or more genuine specimens (most specimens per signer: 1); the manifest has no signing-date column and each specimen was cut from the signer's cheque, so there are no independent genuine queries: genuine acceptance and false rejection are NOT MEASURABLE
0 skilled forgeries (the manifest records no forger); the 240 'forged' rows are script-generated stroke edits of the specimen itself: false acceptance of skilled forgeries is NOT MEASURABLE
240 synthetic alterations are reported only as edited-copy detection, never as forgeries
the test split of this dataset was used repeatedly while the signature model was developed: treat any number taken from it as exploratory

allowed: Edited copies of an enrolled specimen (synthetic stroke additions or erasures) are detected by an alignment check; the counts are in reports/final/MODEL_EVALUATION.md. This is tamper-evidence for copied images, not forgery detection.
On a single-reference baseline with simulated re-captures, signatures of different signers are separated by the similarity score (same report).
not_allowed: Any genuine-acceptance or false-rejection rate for real signers.
Any statement about resistance to skilled forgery.
Population-level accuracy: every signer has one specimen, so no signer can be evaluated with independent signatures.
Detection of forgeries on the strength of synthetic alterations: those are edits of a specimen and may only be cited as edited-copy detection.
Performance on whole cheques, other scanners, or signatures captured differently from the evaluation data.
Suitability for production use: this protocol measures one component on one data set.
